text: Themistocles replied, that a man's discourse was like to a rich Persian carpet, the beautiful figures and patterns of which can only be shown by spreading and extending it out; when it is contracted and folded up, they are obscured and lost; and, therefore, he desired time.
author: Plutarch
speaker: Themistocles
translation: John Dryden et al., rev. Arthur Hugh Clough, 1864
